transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

From what you have described, the most likely cause is reseat the water container and check its detection; confirm condensate is actually being produced. Slide the water container out, empty it, check it isn't cracked and that the lid / float is clean, then push it firmly all the way home until it clicks. Was it full or not pushed fully in (and is it sorted), is it cracked, or was it already empty, seated and fine?
It was already nearly empty and I've pushed it in firmly until it clicks, still does it. The filter/sieve on the container was slimy so I cleaned that too. Still stops 20-40 mins in.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is clear the condensate path / sump of fluff-sludge (and clean the condenser). Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]

Condenser and fluff filters are cleaned, they were fairly clean. I also found a small cover near the condenser with grey slimy water and fluff behind it, wiped what I could reach. It then ran about an hour but the light came on again.
Is the container actually staying empty with water pooling elsewhere, and is the condenser/sump clear of fluff?

The container stays nearly empty, I can't see water pooling anywhere. The sump bit had grey slimy water and fluff which I wiped out as far as I could reach, but I can't get round the back or move it as it's stacked on the washer. Any idea what's wrong?

It likely depends on a faulty moisture sensor or water level switch that is incorrectly detecting liquid despite the tank being empty. You may need to replace these internal components as standard cleaning has not resolved the issue. Run a normal drying programme. Is it collecting the water (and staying dry underneath) now, or still not?
So is it a faulty sensor then? I did wipe the moisture sensor bars already. I can't get at the back or pull it out, and I haven't got a multimeter. What can I actually do from the front?

It could be a faulty moisture sensor, but it might also be a blockage in the drainage or circulation system. From the front, you can try running a hot wash cycle with a dishwasher cleaner to dissolve any remaining slime and ensure the filter is perfectly clean. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
